run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:45:44Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert is about sporadic frontend-proxy request errors. In the observed span metrics, frontend-proxy error spans were low and intermittent (ingress 5-minute error ratio 0.0003–0.0029 between 23:16 and 00:00), with one distinct burst of 13 error spans between 23:39:30 and 23:40:00 (7 ingress + 6 'router frontend egress'). At the same moment the frontend service error-span counter jumped by 25, including 6 new grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client errors and 5 failed GET /api/products/{productId} requests, re-implicating product-catalog as the failing dependency. The product-catalog Deployment was rolled out at 23:38:19–23:38:23Z (pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp replaced by product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9) with the same image and env and only a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:38:19Z template annotation (revision 2). The flagd-config ConfigMap holds the only switched-on fault-injection setting found (productCatalogFailure = on, 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product'), which refers to exactly the restarted dependency whose GetProduct calls failed; no other object was seen applying a fault to product-catalog. The declared fault itself was not directly observed (product-catalog logged 'Product Found' and reported no error-status spans, and the GetProduct error counter stayed flat at 6 after 23:40), and the timing of the flag change is unknown, so the conclusion is partial. Separately, chronic low-rate 503s from frontend-proxy to the 'frontend' upstream (response flag UC, upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}) predate and postdate the burst and are background, not proven impact of the product-catalog change.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans were low and intermittent, with one clear burst: the cumulative error-span counter for service_name="frontend-proxy" went 956 (23:25) → 966 (23:39) with 1–3 increments, jumped 966 → 979 (+13) between samples at 23:39:30 and 23:40:00, then rose only +1 at 23:45, +1 at 23:46, +1 at 23:51, +1 at 23:54 and +2 at 23:55.
Per-operation breakdown of that burst: frontend-proxy ingress error spans 519 (23:39:30) → 526 (23:40:00) = +7 and 'router frontend egress' error spans 447 → 453 = +6.

In the same interval the frontend service error-span counter rose 1819 → 1844 (+25), including a new series for span_name="grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" with status STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 6, GET /api/products/{productId} at 5, 'executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]' at 5, tcp.connect 28→29, POST 70→71, POST /api/checkout 69→70 and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 69→70.
The frontend's ProductCatalogService/GetProduct error counter stayed exactly at 6 from 23:40:00 through 00:01:00 — the product-catalog call failures did not recur during the remaining ~25 minutes.

frontend-proxy access logs record 503 responses with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} forwarded to the 'frontend' cluster, e.g. 23:38:19.360Z, 23:39:13.331Z and 23:53:49.003Z/23:53:49.621Z.

Trace 6813a7c1ce024c38c1742bc4ad008baa (23:31:34) shows load-generator GET 503 (otel.status_code=ERROR) → frontend-proxy 'ingress' 503 (otel.status_code=ERROR) → 'router frontend egress' with tag error="true" and http.status_code=0, i.e. the proxy→frontend hop produced no response.

The sampled frontend-proxy error traces (5 traces spanning 23:31:17–23:33:23) all show operation 'ingress' with error=true/http.status_code=503/otel.status_code=ERROR totalling 5 error rows, plus 5 matching 'router frontend egress' spans with error="true"/http.status_code=0.

frontend-proxy ingress error ratio per 5 minutes over 23:16–00:00 ranged from 0.00029 to 0.00289, peaking at the samples covering 23:40:00–23:44:00 (0.00289 at 23:40, 0.00263 at 23:41, 0.00233 at 23:42/23:43, 0.00203 at 23:44) and back to 0.00029 at 23:45.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo record a rollout of Deployment product-catalog at 23:38:19–23:38:23Z: 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1', pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started (23:38:19–23:38:22), and 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0' with Pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp Killing at 23:38:23.

The product-catalog Deployment's pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:38:19Z (metadata generation 2, observedGeneration 2, revision 2), while both ReplicaSets product-catalog-55f64b54c9 and product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc specify the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog and identical container env (FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, PRODUCT_CATALOG_PORT=8080, GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB), i.e. a restart with an otherwise unchanged pod template.

Current state: pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 is Running/ready with 0 restarts; the product-catalog Deployment reports ready=1 and available=1; all 21 otel-demo Deployments report ready=1/available=1, and all 21 listed otel-demo pods are Running with restarts=0 and no lastState termination.
product-catalog container logs around the burst (23:39:20–23:40:10Z) show repeated 'Product Found' lines (e.g. 23:40:05.760Z through 23:40:09.835Z).
product-catalog span metrics for 23:45–00:05 contain only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET (8310 spans per 20m); no product-catalog spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR appear in the returned series.

ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo, key demo.flagd.json, created 2026-11-17T23:05:17Z) contains the only switched-on fault-injection setting read: productCatalogFailure with "defaultVariant": "on", "state": "ENABLED", description "Fail product catalog service on a specific product"; the other flags in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) are all "off".

The flagd-config setting productCatalogFailure=on is the only object seen holding a fault/injection setting that refers to product-catalog, the workload that was restarted at 23:38:19Z with an unchanged pod template and whose GetProduct calls failed (6 frontend client errors) in the 23:39:30–23:40:00 burst; no other object in otel-demo shows a fault applied to product-catalog.

frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw is ready with 0 restarts and lastState null (no OOMKilled/terminated instance), created 23:05:17Z; its service endpoints point to that pod (100.96.3.42), and product-catalog endpoints point to product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 (100.96.4.33).

The alert annotation value 0.011111… (=1/90) is consistent with the 13 frontend-proxy error spans in the one-minute window covering 23:39:30–23:40:00 against roughly 1150–1170 frontend-proxy spans per minute (23,021 ingress+egress spans per 20 min), whereas every other 5-minute ratio computed was 0.0003–0.0029; the actual alert expression could not be read.

The 23:39:30–23:40:00 frontend failures (6 ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client errors, 5 failed product-page requests, 1 tcp.connect error) are most plausibly transient gRPC connectivity failures caused by the product-catalog pod replacement that completed at 23:38:23Z (old pod killed, new pod started), with the frontend's channel to the terminated pod failing on the next product requests.

frontend-proxy 503s to the 'frontend' upstream occurred before the product-catalog rollout and after the burst as well (23:22:31, 23:26:09, 23:27:07, 23:31:17, 23:31:34, 23:36:11, 23:38:19, 23:39:13, 23:53:49), so a chronic background of frontend-proxy request errors independent of the 23:38 product-catalog change exists and cannot be attributed to it.

product-catalog is not broadly failing: it reports no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, its pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts, and its logs at the time of the burst show 'Product Found' lines rather than errors.

A persistent per-product product-catalog failure (as the flag description implies) was not observed to recur: the frontend's GetProduct error counter is flat at 6 from 23:40:00 to 00:01:00, despite ~4900 GET /api/products/{productId} spans per 20 minutes continuing in the same period.
Rejected: a frontend pod crash, OOM or restart as the cause of the frontend-proxy 503s — the frontend pod is ready with restartCount 0, lastState null and no previous container instance.

Rejected: node pressure / eviction / OOMKilled damage across otel-demo — no Evicted or OOMKilled events appear; the only otel-demo events are the product-catalog rollout (ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing), and all 21 pods are Running, ready, with 0 restarts.

Verify the effective flagd value for productCatalogFailure (flagd-ui or flagd OFREP) and reset it to "off" if product-catalog failures are not intended; also review who/what applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T23:38:19Z to Deployment product-catalog via cluster audit/change history, which is not available in this Run.

Obtain the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition from the alerting layer that produced it: the Prometheus queried in this Run returned no matching alerting rule (the RequestErrorRate rule query and the alert-type list both came back empty, no_data views), so the metric, denominator and window behind the reported 0.011111 could not be confirmed.

gaps: The alert's own expression could not be verified: the list_prometheus_rules query for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing and the alert-type rule listing returned nothing (both no_data views); nothing can be concluded from those empty results about whether the rule exists elsewhere or what its metric, denominator and window are.

Jaeger access limits in this Run: traces_search for service frontend in 23:38–23:43 returned nothing, traces_search_by_tags error=true for frontend in 23:35–23:46 returned nothing, and the frontend-proxy error-trace sample only covered 23:31:17–23:33:23, so the traces of the 23:39:30–23:40:00 failures could not be read.

The frontend container's logs in 23:20–00:05 were not obtainable: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw returned no content (0 bytes read, status no_data), so frontend-side error text for the failed product-page requests is unknown.

product-catalog error logs for individual GetProduct failures are unavailable: a filtered search for err|error|fail|panic|fatal in 23:30–23:54 matched nothing (no_data, not proof of absence), and the replaced pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp no longer exists so its logs cannot be read; which product ID failed is unknown.

The declared fault of productCatalogFailure ('Fail product catalog service on a specific product') was not directly observed: no product-catalog error-status spans, no error log lines, and the 6 GetProduct errors did not recur after 23:40.

It cannot be determined when flagd-config's productCatalogFailure was switched to 'on' (the ConfigMap only shows creationTimestamp 2026-11-17T23:05:17Z) or who/what issued the kubectl rollout restart annotation at 23:38:19Z — the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
The single frontend tcp.connect error span in the burst has no available trace, so its target dependency is unknown.
The kubernetes networkpolicies query for otel-demo returned no items (no_data view); that cannot prove no NetworkPolicy affected these connections during the window.

There is a mismatch between metrics and access logs for the burst: metrics show +7 frontend-proxy ingress error spans between 23:39:30 and 23:40:00, while Envoy access logs in 23:39:00–23:40:10 show only one 503 (23:39:13) and no 5xx responses (only 200 responses with 404-byte bodies for POST /api/checkout); the reason (span/log export timing or sampling) is unknown.

The frontend-proxy log reads used here were truncated or read-limited (2940cd1b-9467-4830-ad23-877662512d3f-t0 read only through 23:40:17.253327Z, and 80507d72-3ca7-4b4f-9d6c-3e4f60cb3304-t1 and 15998216-0e14-4519-83e8-8aeed93ac774-t1 showed only their newest matching lines), so lines outside those reads are unknown.
